div.head: Hn 17.2
div.ab: De essartis; de cesione; de combustione; de uenacione; de gestacione arcus et iaculorum in foresta; de misera canum expeditacione; si quis ad stabilitam non uenit; si quis pecu[ni]am suam reclusam dimisit; de edificiis in foresta; de summonicionibus supersessis; de obuiacione alicuius in foresta cum canibus; de corio uel carne inuenta.

Vgl. Gl Jagd 6 ff.; Wilhelm von Malmesbury Reg. II § 196 erwähnt stabulata, quibus in casses cervi urgentur unter Eadward III. Den folgenden Fall übersetzt Stubbs (Lect. 158): ‘leaves his stock shut up’; ich verstehe: ‘sein Stallvieh [in den Forst] laufen liess’.—Die versäumten Summonitiones ergingen nicht bloss an die Parteien, sondern auch an die arg durch Häufigkeit von Forstprozessen bedrückten Urteilfinder; vgl. Petit-Dut. Mél. Bémont 70—pecuram{46} s. r. d.; de sumonic. ohne de c. in f.—coriis{50} Rs

Cf. Gl Jagd 6 ff.; William of Malmesbury Reg. II § 196 mentions stabulata, quibus in casses cervi urgentur under Eadward III. The following case is translated by Stubbs (Lect. 158) as ‘leaves his stock shut up’; I understand it as ‘let his stall-cattle run loose [into the forest]’.—The neglected Summonitiones were issued not only to the parties but also to the doomsmen, who were sorely burdened by the frequency of forest suits; cf. Petit-Dut. Mél. Bémont 70—pecuram{46} s. r. d.; de sumonic. without de c. in f.—coriis{50} Rs
